status: REVIEW ROUND 1 response. Test split NOT re-touched this round, per reviewer instruction ('test split stays untouched until the final measurement'). All results below are val. The round-1 test measurement is retained further down as a superseded historical record (it was measured honestly at the time, but used a model trained on 0.8% of the corpus and is now known to be a loose upper bound on error, not a ceiling).

corrections_to_spec.velocity_present_claim: Spec states velocity_present is false everywhere. Measured on the full split=train table: mvd (752,249,168 rows, 93% of the table) has velocity_present=false / vx null for 100% of rows -- spec is RIGHT here. qwd (55,031,703 rows) has velocity_present=true with real vx/vy/vz for 23,836,754 rows (43.3% of qwd, the recording-POV rows) -- spec is WRONG here. An earlier revision of this file inverted the mvd half of this statement (claimed velocity_present=true for mvd); that was backwards from both the spec and the data and is corrected here. Methodology is unaffected either way: this module finite-differences positions uniformly regardless of the native velocity columns.

row_counts.train_note: full split=train, all 2,449 demos, no demo-level subsampling (round 1 used demo_cap=300, 0.8% of the 807M-row corpus); row_cap=50,000,000 per horizon via post-hoc random subsample of the full 646.9M/H=300 (resp. H=600) candidate population, not reservoir sampling (see pipeline/predict_enemy.py _stage_paired docstring for the measured reservoir-sampling bug this replaced).
row_counts.val_note: full split=val, all 176 demos, row_cap=10,000,000 per horizon.

data_only_model_r2.description: Same architecture family as round 1 (256 width) but depth=3 (136,195 params -- a round-1/round-2 midpoint caused by a CLI-default bug caught during this run, kept as a useful isolated 'more data alone, ~same size' data point), trained on the same 100M-row set.

view_angle_ablation_model_r2_ablate.description: Same architecture as primary_model_r2_big (534,531 vs 532,995 params -- the difference is exactly the dropped input columns' first-layer weights) but with dyaw_view/sin_vp/cos_vp removed, retrained on the full 100M-row set to re-check round 1's ablation finding at this data scale.
view_angle_ablation_model_r2_ablate.architecture: MLP 11->512->512->512->3, ReLU, SmoothL1(beta=5.0) loss on frame-space offset

summary_val_h300_median_u.note: More data alone (round1's architecture at 100M rows) moves the H=300 median from ~35.1u to ~33.0u; adding the architecture scale-up (256->512 width) moves it further to ~32.5u. View-angle features contribute ~1.1-1.5u at every scale tried (round 1: 35.1 vs 36.2 at 70k params/5.86M rows; round 2: 32.5 vs 33.7 at 533k params/100M rows) -- real, reproducible, but not close to closing a 12-16u gap to any of the candidate direct-hit/rocket-splash thresholds. The remaining gap looks like a feature-set ceiling, not a data- or capacity-starved one: train loss is flat at the end of every run in both rounds.

historical_round_1_test_measurement_SUPE.note: Test split touched once under round 1's rules, before the data/model scale was known to be a live question. Retained for transparency, not as a current result -- do not compare against round 2's val numbers on gate terms; the model here is undertrained by round 2's own finding.
historical_round_1_test_measurement_SUPE.architecture: MLP 14->256->256->3, ReLU, SmoothL1(beta=5.0) loss on frame-space offset

gate_computed_at_the_time.note: This gate (16u direct-hit fire_tolerance derived margin) is itself under review -- see spec REVIEW ROUND 1. No gate is computed for round 2's results above; only the raw distribution is reported, per reviewer instruction.
